newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU cuts 1997/98 grain public storage payments.
newsitem.headline: EU cuts 1997/98 grain public storage payments.

text.p: European Union farm ministers agreed on Wednesday to cut monthly payments for cereals held in intervention stores to 1.0 Ecus a tonne in 1997/98 (July/June) from 1.1 Ecus a tonne in 1996/97, EU officials said.
The reduction, part of an annual farm price package, takes account of lower interest rates and storage costs.

Cereals intervention prices are raised each month between November and end-May to take account of storage costs and to discourage farmers and merchants from selling into intervention stores at the earliest opportunity. Southern member states and Sweden have a slightly different schedule.
EU cereals intervention prices remain unchanged at 119.19 Ecus a tonne.
The moisture content for cereals going into intervention stores will be maintained at 15 percent in 1997/98.
An exemption for Finland and Sweden on the minimum size of barley grain accepted for intervention was extended for another two years.
